Excluded and assumption-sensitive source questions

These records are retained for source criticism, not counted as practice questions. Ambiguous assumptions, missing correct alternatives and alternative valid implementations must not be silently repaired. No official-key verification is claimed.

Phd CS 1404 Q67 — Collision probability with replacement

Original PDF · page 15 · Q67

An urn contains N balls numbered 1 through N. Draw n balls without replacement. What is the probability that at least one ball is selected twice? These are the alternatives printed in the supplied scan.

  1. 1/Nn
  2. 1-1/N!
  3. (Nn)/Nn
  4. 1-N!/(n!Nn)

Independent audit and practice decision

  1. Without replacement, the same ball cannot be selected twice. Thus for a valid experiment with n≤N, the stated probability is zero.
  2. None of the printed expressions is identically zero. The question's wording and alternatives are therefore inconsistent. We do not silently change “without” into “with.”
  3. If replacement had been intended, the collision probability would instead be 1-N!/((N-n)!Nn). The printed fourth denominator is n!Nn, so even that reinterpretation would need a second correction.
  4. This source record is excluded from practice, but retained as an example of checking experiment rules before applying a memorized formula.

MS CE 1405 Q77 — Minimum NOR realization

Original PDF · page 16 · Q77

Each input variable and its complement are available. What minimum NOR-gate combination realizes F=x(y⊕z)¯+yz¯?

  1. Four two-input NOR gates and one three-input NOR gate.

  2. Five two-input NOR gates and one three-input NOR gate.

  3. Three two-input NOR gates and one three-input NOR gate.

  4. Two two-input NOR gates and two three-input NOR gates.

Independent audit and practice decision

  1. Expanding and simplifying gives
F=xy+xz¯+yz¯=(x+y)(x+z¯)(y+z¯)

. 2. Three two-input NOR gates complement the pair sums; one three-input NOR combines them. This gives the conventional option 3 construction. 3. The source does not state whether redundant tied pins count as a three-input gate. If they do, replace one of the first-stage two-input NORs with a three-input NOR having one repeated input. The function is unchanged and the gate counts now match option 4, also totaling four gates. 4. Thus a unique fan-in-count answer needs an additional convention. We retain the construction as a tutorial and exclude the printed question from unique-answer practice. Its logical function remains useful for original questions with an explicit gate model.

MS CE 1405 Q78 — A hazard-free SOP with unspecified cells

Original PDF · page 16 · Q78

For

F(a,b,c,d)=∏M(2,3,4,10,11,12,13,14)

with don't-care indices 0 and 1, which is the simplified SOP so that it is hazard-free? Index order is a,b,c,d.

  1. a¯bc+bcd+b¯c¯+a¯c¯d
  2. a¯bd+a¯bc+bcd+b¯c¯
  3. a¯bd+a¯bc+bcd+ab¯c¯
  4. a¯bd+a¯bc+bcd+a¯c¯

Independent audit and practice decision

  1. The required one-set is {5,6,7,8,9,15}. Specified zero cells must remain zero; don't-care cells 0 and 1 may be chosen freely.
  2. Option 2 covers the adjacent required-one pairs 5–7, 6–7, 7–15 and 8–9 with common implicants. It has eleven literals and includes the four-cell group {0,1,8,9}.
  3. Option 1 lacks common coverage for transition 5–7 and can have a static-one hazard. Option 4 misses required ones 8 and 9. Option 3 preserves the required outputs and covers every required-one adjacency when don't-cares 0 and 1 are assigned zero, but has twelve literals; its group covering 8 and 9 is not prime once the don't-cares are available for expansion.
  4. The source also asks for a simplified expression. Interpreting that as minimum-literal prime-implicant coverage selects option 2; interpreting the question as hazard freedom alone admits option 3 as well. This is a convention-sensitive item, not proof that the conventional simplified answer is wrong. We exclude it from unqualified single-answer practice and state the minimization convention in original exercises.
